desc: Former data storage services company that provided managed storage to enterprises from its own data centres during the dot-com era.
markets: US managed storage provider in the early 2000s; the company was wound down after its Nasdaq listing.
rationale: Company no longer exists, so it has no sponsorship capacity or brand to promote through F1.

name: Neonode
desc: Swedish developer and licensor of zForce optical sensing for touch, gesture and presence detection in printers, e-readers and cars.
markets: Licenses and sells sensing modules to manufacturers in Europe, North America and Asia, mainly printers and automotive makers.
rationale: Small licensing and sensor firm with automotive interest; limited marketing budget and weak F1 fit.

name: Smoore Technology
desc: Chinese manufacturer of vaping hardware, best known for ceramic-coil atomisation, supplying devices, pods and cartridges to vaping and tobacco brands.
markets: Supplies vaping devices and components to brands in North America, Europe and Asia, including major tobacco groups.
rationale: Nicotine-sector supplier faces marketing restrictions and sells mostly to other brands, so F1 sponsorship is very unlikely.
f1: Supplies vaping hardware to British American Tobacco (F1 partner)

name: WPS Office (Kingsoft Office)
desc: Developer of the WPS Office suite offering word processing, spreadsheets and presentations compatible with Microsoft Office on desktop and mobile.

rationale: Consumer and enterprise software brand seeking international growth, and Microsoft already in F1 as a rival; some audience fit.

name: Yuntianmall.com
desc: Nanjing company classed by Crunchbase under consumer electronics, with a name suggesting an online electronics shop.

name: Zepp
desc: Wearables company that began as Zepp Labs, making motion-sensing sensors and apps for sports training such as golf swing analysis.

rationale: Consumer wearables brand with a sports audience, similar to WHOOP's F1 deal; entity is uncertain and budget unknown.

name: eCobalt Solutions
desc: Former Canadian mining developer working on the Idaho Cobalt Project to produce cobalt for batteries and other uses.
markets: Developed a single project in Idaho, United States, with no production or sales; the company is no longer active.
rationale: Pre-revenue developer of one mine with no consumer brand; no realistic F1 fit.

name: Keeson Technology
desc: Chinese manufacturer of smart adjustable beds, mattresses and related furniture for global retailers and its own brands.
markets: Sells adjustable beds and mattresses to furniture retailers in North America, Europe and Asia, much of it as a manufacturer for others.
rationale: Largely a manufacturer supplying other brands, with limited own-brand marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Ningbo Joyson Electronic
desc: Chinese automotive electronics and safety group making steering wheels, airbags, seat belts, infotainment and driver-assist electronics.
markets: Supplies carmakers in Europe, North America and Asia, including through its Joyson Safety Systems operations.
rationale: Tier-1 automotive supplier with global plants; safety and electronics expertise gives a technology tie-in, but B2B brand awareness is modest.

name: Roborock
desc: Chinese maker of robot vacuum cleaners and mops, plus handheld wet-dry vacuums and robotic lawn products.
markets: Sells under its own brand in over 100 countries, including strong presence in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Global consumer appliance brand with international growth and product-launch needs; F1's affluent global audience is a plausible reach channel.

name: Hundsun Technologies
desc: Chinese financial software and services group supplying trading, securities, asset management and banking systems to brokers, banks and asset managers.
markets: Customers are mainly Chinese brokers, banks, fund managers and exchanges; overseas business is small.
rationale: B2B financial software vendor with domestic customers; limited consumer marketing and weak F1 fit.

name: Plastic Logic Germany
desc: Dresden operation of Plastic Logic, which developed flexible plastic electronics and organic thin-film transistor displays such as e-paper screens.

rationale: Likely inactive or small component business with no marketing profile; weak F1 fit.

name: ION Investment Group
desc: Financial technology and data company supplying trading, treasury, workflow, analytics and risk software to banks, corporates and asset managers.
markets: Sells financial software and data to banks, corporates and asset managers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Enterprise fintech group with global clients where F1 B2B hospitality could serve client entertainment; limited consumer branding.

name: Silicor Materials
desc: Former solar-grade silicon producer that developed an aluminium-alloy process for polysilicon, with a planned plant in Iceland.

desc: Chip design subsidiary of telecom equipment maker ZTE, also called Sanechips, designing semiconductors for communications and consumer products.
markets: Supplies chips mainly to ZTE and other Chinese device and network equipment makers; overseas sales are not confirmed.
rationale: Captive chip arm of a telecom group with no consumer brand of its own; weak F1 fit.

markets: US-based data centre chip developer; it was acquired and folded into Microsoft's data centre engineering in 2023.

markets: Sells chips to camera makers mainly in China, with exports to overseas device makers likely but unconfirmed.

name: SmartSens Technology
desc: Shanghai fabless designer of CMOS image sensors used in security cameras, smartphones, cars and machine vision.
markets: Sells image sensors to camera, phone and automotive makers, mainly in China and Asia, with overseas customers likely but unconfirmed.
rationale: Component maker with no consumer brand; image-sensor technology links loosely to broadcast, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Density
desc: Company making people-counting sensors and software that give workplaces, buildings and campuses real-time occupancy data.
markets: US-based workplace analytics supplier selling to corporate and real estate customers, mainly in North America.
rationale: Workplace analytics vendor that could use B2B hospitality for corporate clients, but small and US-focused.

name: Medsphere Systems
desc: Healthcare IT company supplying electronic health record software, including CareVue and OpenVista, to community hospitals and behavioural health providers.
markets: Sells to US community hospitals and behavioural health providers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Niche US healthcare IT vendor with no consumer marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Cloud Imperium Games
desc: Video game developer behind Star Citizen, a persistent space simulation, and the single-player campaign Squadron 42, largely crowdfunded.
markets: Studios in the US, UK and Germany, with players worldwide buying the game online.
rationale: Simulation game brand with an engaged fan community; racing and space-sim crossover and F1 gaming audience offer plausible activation.
